did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a painful question: Why does the Lord seem to stand far away and hide his face precisely in times of trouble? This expresses the worshiper’s distress, not a claim that the Lord is actually absent.
The verse contrasts the wicked person’s pride with the poor person’s situation: the wicked pursue the poor, who may be caught in the schemes devised against them.

The wicked person is portrayed as boasting about his heart’s desires. The verse links praise of desire and greed with contempt for the Lord, presenting moral corruption not only as harm to other people but also as rebellion against faith.
The wicked person lives with the feeling that his ways always prosper and that the Lord’s judgments have no power over him. His self-confidence also leads him to treat his enemies with contempt.

The wicked person’s mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression, while his tongue conceals trouble and wrongdoing. The image emphasizes that the vulnerable are harmed not only through actions but also through misleading and hurtful speech.
The wicked person acts in ambush and secrecy: he lies in wait in the villages, seeking to attack the innocent, and watches for the vulnerable in order to exploit their helplessness.
The chapter compares the wicked person to a lion waiting in its den and seeking to seize the poor. It also uses the image of a net, emphasizing both the deception and the trapping of the vulnerable.

The wicked person says in his heart that God has forgotten, hidden his face, and will never see. This expresses the wicked person’s inner conviction that there is no justice or providence, not the psalmist’s own view.
The psalmist emphasizes that the Lord does see trouble and suffering. He presents the Lord as the helper of the orphan and as the one to whom the vulnerable can entrust their cause.

At the end of the prayer, the tone changes: after describing the wicked and the suffering, the Lord is proclaimed King forever and ever. It then says that he hears the desire of the humble, strengthens their hearts, and brings justice for the oppressed so that they will no longer be terrorized.
